regions.region: page 1 title, abstract, author block, keywords, and SI footnote
regions.finding: Article identity and aggregate highly trans-selective coupling-cyclization claim were inspected. The page says SI is available online, but workspace source mapping leaves SI association unestablished; no SI facts were used.

Earlier amino-alcohol routes and the authors' earlier N-allenyl-amide/coupling work are cited background. No uniquely specified cited experiment with complete row-level conditions is created from this prose.

regions.region: page 1 lower-right Results and Discussion beginning
regions.finding: The page introduces the Scheme 1 multistep preparation and the shared Table 1 standard conditions, then reports row-specific yield/selectivity/recovery observations. These statements are linked to the detailed synthesis-stage and ten Table 1 records rather than duplicated.

unresolved: No reaction drawing appears on page 1; exact Scheme 1 structures/conditions and Table 1 rows are resolved using page 2 plus experimental pages.

regions.finding: All five labeled transformations were reconciled with the individual experimental records: Mitsunobu phthalimide substitution, hydrazinolysis, Ritter alternative for R=Ph, benzoylation, and CuI/paraformaldehyde allenylation. Separate substrate batches and arrows are not collapsed.

regions.region: page 2 center-left Table 1 reaction header, entries 1–10, and footnotes a–e
regions.finding: Ten distinct coupling-cyclization rows were retained with shared 1.0/1.2 mmol scale, Pd(PPh3)4 1 mol%, K2CO3 2 equiv, DMF 4 mL, 80 °C, row times, trans yields, crude-NMR trans/cis ratios, and 20%/5% starting-material recoveries in entries 3/8. Entry 4 also has a separate cis-product outcome from page 6.
The crystal structure supports the trans assignment of 6da but is characterization, not another reaction experiment.
Three optically active substrate experiments were retained separately because substrate ee, reaction time, yield, dr, and product ee differ: (S)-4f, (S)-4b, and (S)-4e with PhI.
The Pd/oxygen-anion sequence is explicitly a rationale for diastereoselectivity and is classified as mechanism; Int is not treated as an isolated preparation.

unresolved: Scheme 2 omits scale, absolute amounts, workup, purification, mass, and analytical bases.
All complex structures and stereochemical encodings remain machine-unverified.

regions.finding: Shared solvent drying, Schlenk-tube, chromatography, and analytical conventions were inspected as general methods; they are not independent reactions.

regions.region: page 3 left column Typical Procedure I for 1a to 2a to 3a
regions.finding: Mitsunobu formation of the phthalimide intermediate, hydrazinolysis to crude 2a, and benzoylation to 3a were retained as three distinct arrows. The 13% value is explicitly total yield from 1a to 3a and not a benzoylation-stage yield.

regions.region: page 3 lower-left to upper-right CuI homologation 3a to 4a
regions.finding: The CuI/paraformaldehyde/Cy2NH/1,4-dioxane experiment was retained separately with argon, 100 °C, 12 h, workup, purification, 0.46 g, and 67% isolated yield.

The DIAD and DEAD Mitsunobu batches are two distinct experiments; their products are combined only for the later hydrazinolysis. Hydrazinolysis, benzoylation to 3b (15% total from 1b), and allenylation to 4b (55%) remain separate records.
The 4c Mitsunobu experiment begins here and continues on page 4; it is represented once with cross-page evidence.

unresolved: Crude 2a/2b masses, yields, and purities are absent.
Stage-only yields for benzoylations reported as multistep total yields remain unknown.

regions.finding: Hydrazinolysis, benzoylation to 3c (16% total from 1c), and CuI homologation to 4c (38%) were retained as distinct transformations, completing the cross-page Mitsunobu record.
The Ritter acetamide formation, 1.2 N HCl hydrolysis to crude amine 2d, benzoylation to 3d (48% total from 1d), and allenylation to 4d (65%) were retained as four separate experiments.

Two separately performed DIAD Mitsunobu batches were retained independently; their combined product then enters distinct hydrazinolysis, benzoylation to 3e (31% total), and allenylation to 4e (64%) records.

unresolved: Crude amine yields and purities are not reported.
Multistep total yields do not reveal isolated benzoylation-stage yields.

regions.finding: Mitsunobu, hydrazinolysis, benzoylation to 3f (16% total from 1f), and CuI homologation to 4f (60%) were retained as four separate experiments.

regions.region: page 5 lower-left and upper-right enantioenriched (S)-4f preparation
regions.finding: Four stages from (R)-1f (99% ee) to (S)-4f were retained separately. The final 14% is explicitly total yield from (R)-1f and the product is 99% ee; no stage-only allenylation yield was invented.
Four stages from (R)-1b (93% ee) to (S)-4b were retained separately. The final 3% is total yield and product ee is reported as >92%.
Mitsunobu, hydrazinolysis, benzoylation, and CuI homologation from (R)-1e were retained separately; the final characterization continues on page 6.

unresolved: The chiral intermediate-stage percentage yields are not reported.
Exact workups are inherited only where the source explicitly invokes the typical procedure; unprinted SI details were not inferred.

regions.finding: HPLC and spectroscopic characterization completes the existing (S)-4e record and confirms the printed 98% ee; it is not a new preparation.

regions.region: page 6 left column Typical Procedure II and 6aa/6ba/6ca
regions.finding: The detailed procedures for Table 1 entries 1–3 were merged with those table rows, adding exact masses, argon/Schlenk operation, workup/purification where printed, and isolated product masses. Entry 3 retains 20% recovered 4c from Table 1.

Detailed procedures for Table 1 entries 4–7 were merged with the existing rows. Entry 4 separately retains trans-6da (280.5 mg, 86%) and cis-6da (20.2 mg, 6%); entries 5–7 retain their row-specific masses, times, chromatographic eluents, and yields.

unresolved: The 6fb characterization continues onto page 7 and was not imported; pages 7–8 remain outside this coverage claim.
